samples.summary: Stored color values are interpolated into DOCX XML attributes without escaping, while adjacent attributes in the same element are escaped — an arbitrary color string (which this change confirms can be persisted verbatim) yields OOXML injection in the exported document.
samples.evidence: This change is built on the premise that a non-color string can end up stored as `InlineStyle.color` (e.g. the legacy `color: ""` the diff now guards against at paint time, and `defaultColorResolver` passes any string through verbatim at packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:16). The renderer path is now hardened, but the DOCX export path is not: packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:71-77 does `defaultColorResolver(style.color)` then `parts.push(`<w:color w:val="${colorHex.replace('#','')}"/>`)` and the same for `w:fill`, with no `escapeXmlAttr` — even though the very same function escapes `style.fontFamily` two lines earlier (docx-style-map.ts:53-56, with a comment explicitly warning about attribute injection). Vector: an actor who can write a color value that is not from the fixed palette (a collaborator writing the Yorkie Tree style attribute directly via the docs/slides API, or a crafted imported DOCX/PPTX whose color string survives import) sets e.g. `color = '#000" /><w:rStyle w:val="x'`; on export the string closes the element and injects attacker-chosen OOXML into a file other users open. I could not confirm an end-to-end write path that bypasses the palette, hence low confidence, but the escaping asymmetry inside one function is concrete.

samples.summary: No validation/normalisation of `StoredColor` at the store boundary: `applyStyle({ color })` accepts any string and it is persisted as-is, so downstream sinks (DOCX XML, future CSS/HTML sinks) must each defend themselves. This change fixes two sinks (canvas fill, caret) rather than the boundary.
samples.evidence: `defaultColorResolver` returns any string unchanged (color.ts:14-22) and the diff's own task note states an empty string "is stored as a real attribute" — i.e. the persistence layer performs no shape check on color values. Searches found no hex/CSS-color validator anywhere on the docs style-apply path; the fix chosen is per-sink (`|| fallback` in paint-layout.ts and resolveColorAtPosition), which leaves other sinks (docx-style-map.ts:73/77) unprotected. Hardening suggestion: validate/normalise to `#RRGGBB` or a `StoredColor` object at `applyStyle`/serializeInlineStyle so no sink can receive a hostile string.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. docx-style-map.ts:71-78 interpolates `colorHex`/`bgHex` into the `w:val` and `w:fill` XML attributes with only `.replace('#','')` and no XML escaping, while the same function escapes `fontFamily` at lines 53-56 using `escapeXmlAttr` (lines 25-32), whose comment explicitly warns these values come from untrusted PPTX/DOCX imports and user input and can inject attributes. No downstream escaping exists: docx-exporter.ts:217-222 splices the returned rPr string in raw, and grep shows escapeXmlAttr is used nowhere else. The stored value is unconstrained: color.ts:12-17 types StoredColor as a bare string and returns it verbatim, with no hex/palette validation anywhere. A concrete untrusted write path exists — import/docx-style-map.ts:59-63 assigns `style.color = '#' + val` from a parsed attribute value (entities already decoded), rejecting only the literal 'auto', so a crafted DOCX with an encoded quote/angle-bracket sequence round-trips into the export and closes the element to inject attacker-chosen OOXML into a file other users open. This is unsafe input handling / markup injection, in the security lens's injection lane, and no guard makes it unreachable.
